html:
The Civil Rights Act of 1964 is the US law that banned discrimination by race, colour, religion, sex or national origin, and ended legal segregation in public places.

It came out of the civil rights movement. Sit ins, boycotts and marches, and the violent response to them in the South, pushed the issue onto national television. President John F. Kennedy proposed the bill in June 1963, and Martin Luther King Jr. and others held the great March on Washington that August.

After Kennedy was killed, Lyndon B. Johnson made the bill his cause. Southern senators blocked it with the longest filibuster in Senate history, about two months, before it passed. Johnson signed it on 2 July 1964.

  • It ended "whites only" hotels, restaurants and other public places.
  • It banned job discrimination and set up a commission to enforce that.
  • It let the government cut federal money to segregated schools and programmes.

It dismantled the Jim Crow system that Brown v. Board of Education had begun to attack. The Voting Rights Act of 1965 followed a year later.
sum: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 is the US law that banned discrimination by race, colour, religion, sex or national origin, and ended legal segregation in public places.
